methodological_rigor.justification: The manuscript presents a de novo genetically engineered H3.3K27M-altered DMG model in human brainstem organoids, with detailed protocols for organoid patterning, electroporation parameters, and microglia incorporation. It evaluates GD2 CAR T cell function longitudinally with multi-modal readouts including imaging, cytokine profiling, and single-cell RNA-seq with explicit QC and integration workflows (for example Seurat clustering, adjusted P-value thresholds for markers, and cross-dataset mapping). For treatment effects in organoids, it uses appropriate modeling (for example a linear mixed-effects model with FDR adjustment across time points for tumor-area reduction comparisons). Limitations include model-system constraints (organoid and engineered tumor context) and relatively small n in some experiments (for example n=2 DMGOs for representative imaging panels), which can affect robustness for certain endpoints.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical model-development and mechanistic immunotherapy study (organoids with engineered DMG plus CAR T cell exposure), so Oxford LoE is 5. Clinical relevance is high because it targets a lethal pediatric tumor (diffuse midline glioma) and directly studies GD2 CAR T cell functional states over prolonged exposure, explicitly linking observed dysfunction patterns to reported clinical outcomes. The addition of myeloid cells to generate DMG-specific microglia and the demonstrated reduction in CAR T efficacy provides translationally meaningful insight into microenvironment-mediated resistance and toxicity mechanisms.

reporting_quality.justification: The work spans organoid engineering, in vitro immunotherapy modeling, and some murine work, so no single listed checklist fits perfectly; “other” is the most accurate choice. Methods are unusually detailed for experimental parameters (for example electroporation voltages/pulse settings; explicit scRNA-seq QC thresholds; integration approaches) and include concrete statistical approaches (two-tailed t-tests, linear mixed-effects models with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment). The manuscript includes “Source data” callouts, but the normalized text does not provide explicit repository links or accession identifiers for raw sequencing datasets, limiting a full reproducibility audit. Overall reporting is strong in methods detail but only moderate in explicit data/code sharing transparency in the provided version.

novelty_literature.justification: The central novelty is an FGF4-driven human brainstem organoid platform engineered to generate infiltrative H3.3K27M-altered DMG with patient-like intratumoral heterogeneity. Using this system for months-long GD2 CAR T exposure to recover and profile divergent effector versus dysfunctional CAR T states goes beyond incremental modeling and creates a new experimental window for mechanism discovery. The incorporation of myeloid cells to generate DMG-specific microglia that measurably suppress CAR T efficacy adds an additional novel microenvironment dimension that is directly relevant to therapeutic resistance.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract concisely states the modeling advances (brainstem organoids, engineered H3.3K27M DMG) and the key experimental finding (microglia reduce GD2 CAR T efficacy and shift functional states). Methods are well organized and provide granular procedural detail that supports replication (cell lines, culture conditions, patterning steps, and analysis toolchains). Some figure-dependent claims rely on references to Extended Data and “Source data” without full context in text, but overall clarity and flow are strong.

key_strengths: Highly detailed and biologically plausible brainstem organoid DMG model enabling prolonged CAR T exposure and mechanistic profiling.
Appropriate quantitative analysis for longitudinal organoid outcomes (linear mixed-effects modeling with multiple-comparison control).
Compelling microenvironment insight: integrated microglia measurably reduces GD2 CAR T tumor control and shifts transcriptional states.
key_concerns: Some experiments have limited sample sizes for specific readouts (for example small n for representative imaging panels), which may reduce confidence in select claims.
The applicable reporting standard is mixed and explicit data/code deposition details are not obvious in the normalized text.
As a preclinical organoid system, external validity to in vivo human disease and clinical CAR T pharmacology remains to be demonstrated.
chief_reviewer.rationale: A novel, high-value preclinical modeling platform with clear translational implications for DMG immunotherapy and microglia-mediated suppression; suitable for a strong translational journal pending minor reporting/transparency clarifications.
